We had a reservation here for Friday night at 9:00pm that we almost didn't make it to. Gladly, two out of three of us made it there after an intense day of day drinking. I wanted so many things on the menu, but my eyes were bigger than my stomach.. so I had to cut down. We started with the Charred Kale Salad - after everything we have been eating in NOLA, I think it's safe to say that we need some greens.

I have to say I have always been at least a little bit smitten by Emeril Despite all his "bams!", which are annoying, I've always found him charming and adorable...or maybe it's just that New Bedford accent and his New England ties that have drawn me in. During my previous New Orleans trip, I met a woman in a wine shop who told me she and her husband would be forever grateful to Emeril. Her husband was a waiter at one of his local restaurants when Katrina hit and damaged the restaurant so that it had to close for a time. After watching Chef Emeril on tv for years, I had to try his restaurant in the heart of NOLA. The inside is so elegant and the service is really nice, quick, and friendly. Everything came out really fast too. The wine and drink selection is nice and tbh the glass of Riesling I had was probably the best glass I've ever had. We got the bbq shrimp for appetizers and it was so good. I'm not really into bbq but the appetizer was amazing. We also got complementary appetizers that had a lobster tart, yuzu oyster and pumpkin soup. I got the lobster entree and it was phenomenal. I love how creole cuisine was elevated.
